references.text: Earlier in the chapter, Moses was angry with the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds—the same ones who now come to him with a gift offering.
Describes the gift that the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds brought to Moses as an atonement offering for the Lord.
Moses' father-in-law Jethro proposed the division into commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, the same military structure mentioned here.
Moses appointed commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds as leaders over the tribes—the same leadership structure found here.
The word 'pekudim' (those who had oversight/commanders) is used in connection with the mustering of Israel's army.
The commanders and their organization of Israel's camp and military forces.
